ai.seo_question: What does it mean when deeds are turned to scattered dust in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Qari'ah is often interpreted as the ultimate nullification of worldly arrogance and material accumulation, reflecting the transient nature of creation (fana) before the eternal reality of God. It serves as a spiritual warning that those who deny the Hereafter will find their efforts dispersed like scattered dust, emphasizing the contrast between temporary worldly power and permanent divine judgment.
